38/G.goal: Explain how to conduct interface and interaction design for an XR system, using the design stage, generic usability rules, and broad interaction categories.
38/G.achieves: Enables the learner to plan the interface and interaction design of an XR system before implementation in the course case study.

38/O1.goal: Describe the initial interface and interaction design process for an XR system, including why it is distinct from code design and how design ideas are represented.
38/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a starting point for turning the design stage into representable design ideas that can be prototyped and evaluated.

38/O2.goal: Explain how generic interface design guidelines, especially Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules, apply to XR interface and interaction design.
38/O2.achieves: Gives the learner usability criteria to evaluate XR interfaces and make design improvements during the system design stage.

38/O3.goal: Identify the broad categories of XR interaction, including object interaction, navigation, and system control.
38/O3.achieves: Gives the learner a taxonomy for describing the interactions an XR system should support in its design.
